summary: A fiction excerpt in which Ray explains how he isolated a suspect's chemical signature from a rat sample near the Whiston suite and used the ship's surveillance net to track the suspect, Freddy, over four days. The footage shows a gap during the critical hours before and after the estimated time of death, while the suspect is otherwise often found at a high-class franchise near the main lift. Becker notes that the evidence is only circumstantial and not enough to bring in a powerful Whiston for questioning.
one_line: Ray tracks a suspect named Freddy through shipboard surveillance, finding a gap around the time of death, but Becker says the circumstantial case is not enough.
key_facts: Ray isolated Freddy's signature by obtaining a rat in the vicinity of the Whiston suite and analyzing it.
Ray used roundabout methods to get a rat near the Whiston suite in full analysis mode, since he did not want to ask for a sample directly.
Ray coded a search of the surveillance net into the regular drone routine after isolating Freddy's signature.
Ray redirected the surveillance net to track Freddy's movements for the last four days.
The footage shows fairly conclusive movements of Freddy before the estimated time of death and activities a few hours after.
The footage contains a big gaping hole in the middle, covering the critical hours.
Freddy is usually found at the franchise during almost any time of day, except during the nightly batch transmission.
The franchise is high class, high price, and exclusive, and it is located right off the main lift.
Ray cut footage of Freddy's less liquid adventures because it was not family friendly viewing.
Freddy has a reputation for being a man who pays handsomely for satisfaction and confidentiality.
Freddy's passenger pre-screen shows no psychological issues, no legal history, and no profile as an incident perpetrator.
Becker says there is no definitive proof, only evidence of absence during the critical hours.
Ray responds that he has pattern, which is the start of a decent circumstantial case.
Becker considers the circumstantial case insufficient to bring in a suspect as powerful as a Whiston for questioning.
Freddy's sister is a Whiston, and Becker grimaces when thinking about her.
